about: Public typical constants that scripts/estimate_impact.py may use ONLY when the user passes --use-defaults, and then always labelled 'PUBLIC TYPICAL VALUE, replace with your own'. None of these is a value for any particular plant. Every value was read from the official file or page named in its entry (downloaded or fetched on the date in 'checked'); nothing here is typed from memory. Values that could not be confirmed from an official US EPA, DOE or EIA source are listed under 'not_included' with the reason. See docs/IMPACT_ESTIMATE.md.

kg_per_lb.note: Exact by definition of the international avoirdupois pound.
kg_per_lb.source: NIST Special Publication 811 (2008), Appendix B; international avoirdupois pound defined as exactly 0.45359237 kg

mmbtu_per_therm.source: US EIA, Natural gas explained: units and conversions (1 therm = 100,000 Btu; 1 dekatherm = 10 therms)

mmbtu_per_dekatherm.note: Exact by definition: 1 dekatherm = 10 therms = 1,000,000 Btu.
mmbtu_per_dekatherm.source: US EIA, Natural gas explained: units and conversions (1 therm = 100,000 Btu; 1 dekatherm = 10 therms)

gwp.source: US EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub (2025), GWP table at the top of the 'Emission Factors Hub' sheet (CH4 28, N2O 265; 'Source: IPCC Fifth Assessment Report (AR5), 2013'); see also its Table 11.
gwp.note: eGRID2023 uses the same basis: its Technical Guide (section on CO2e) states AR5 without climate-carbon feedbacks, CH4 28 and N2O 265.

natural_gas.name: Natural gas (pipeline quality)
natural_gas.cite: US EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub, Table 1 Stationary Combustion
natural_gas.computed_as: kg CO2e = kg CO2 + (g CH4 x 28 + g N2O x 265) / 1000, AR5 GWPs
natural_gas.source: US EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub (2025), Table 1 Stationary Combustion, row 'Natural Gas' (Last Modified: January 15, 2025). The Hub cites 40 CFR Part 98 Tables C-1 and C-2.
natural_gas.scope_note: Combustion emissions only (the Hub: 'do not represent upstream emissions'). Higher heating value basis. The Hub page, fetched 2026-10-29, listed the 2025 edition as the latest.

distillate_fuel_oil_no2.name: Distillate fuel oil No. 2
distillate_fuel_oil_no2.cite: US EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub, Table 1 Stationary Combustion
distillate_fuel_oil_no2.computed_as: kg CO2e = kg CO2 + (g CH4 x 28 + g N2O x 265) / 1000
distillate_fuel_oil_no2.source: US EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub (2025), Table 1 Stationary Combustion, row 'Distillate Fuel Oil No. 2'.

residual_fuel_oil_no6.name: Residual fuel oil No. 6
residual_fuel_oil_no6.cite: US EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub, Table 1 Stationary Combustion
residual_fuel_oil_no6.computed_as: kg CO2e = kg CO2 + (g CH4 x 28 + g N2O x 265) / 1000
residual_fuel_oil_no6.source: US EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub (2025), Table 1 Stationary Combustion, row 'Residual Fuel Oil No. 6'.

propane.name: Propane
propane.cite: US EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub, Table 1 Stationary Combustion
propane.computed_as: kg CO2e = kg CO2 + (g CH4 x 28 + g N2O x 265) / 1000
propane.source: US EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub (2025), Table 1 Stationary Combustion, row 'Propane' (Petroleum Products).

grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.label: US average grid emission rate (eGRID2023 national total output CO2e rate)
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.cite: US EPA eGRID2023 Summary Tables rev. 2, Table 1, U.S. total output CO2e rate
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.computed_as: 770.884 lb CO2e/MWh x 0.45359237 kg/lb / 1000 kWh/MWh = 0.3496671 kg CO2e/kWh (rounded to 7 significant figures)
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.source: US EPA, eGRID2023 Summary Tables (Revision 2), Table 1 Subregion Output Emission Rates, row 'U.S.', total output emission rate CO2e (sheet 'Table 1', cell G32).
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.published: eGRID2023 released January 15, 2025; Revision 2 June 12, 2025. The summary-data page, fetched 2026-10-29, listed 2023 as the latest data year.
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.accounting: Location-based Scope 2 (average emission rate of generation on the grid). Not a market-based factor and not a marginal (avoided-emissions) rate. Excludes transmission and distribution losses (eGRID lists a separate grid gross loss, 4.2% for the U.S.).
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.subregion_spread: Subregion total output CO2e rates in the same table run from 242.776 lb/MWh (NYUP, NPCC Upstate NY) to 1,248.582 lb/MWh (SRMW, SERC Midwest) in the contiguous US, about 5 times, and to 1,548.530 lb/MWh (PRMS, Puerto Rico Miscellaneous). Use your subregion, found by ZIP code in EPA's Power Profiler: https://www.epa.gov/egrid/power-profiler
grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.derived_from_note: The components are eGRID's own published rates, each rounded to three decimals; recombined with GWP 28 and 265 they give 770.925, 0.005% above eGRID's published CO2e rate (770.884). The published rate is used, not the recombination.

electricity_price_per_kwh.label: US average price of electricity to industrial customers, 2025 (8.51 cents/kWh, nominal dollars)
electricity_price_per_kwh.cite: US EIA Electric Power Annual Table 2.4, industrial
electricity_price_per_kwh.source: US EIA, Electric Power Annual, Table 2.4 Average Price of Electricity to Ultimate Customers by End-Use Sectors, 2015 through 2025, row 2025, 'Total Electric Industry', column Industrial: 8.51 cents per kilowatthour. Data for 2025, released October 21, 2026.
electricity_price_per_kwh.license: Public domain (EIA: 'U.S. government publications are in the public domain', https://www.eia.gov/about/copyrights_reuse.php)
electricity_price_per_kwh.note: An average revenue per kWh (energy, demand and fixed charges together) across all US industrial customers. Your marginal energy rate can differ a great deal by state, utility, tariff and time of day.

natural_gas_heat_content_mmbtu_per_mcf.label: US average heat content of natural gas delivered to consumers, 2025 (1,036 Btu per cubic foot)
natural_gas_heat_content_mmbtu_per_mcf.cite: US EIA, heat content of natural gas delivered to consumers, U.S.
natural_gas_heat_content_mmbtu_per_mcf.source: US EIA, Natural Gas Annual data: Heat Content of Natural Gas Consumed, 'Delivered to Consumers', U.S., 2025: 1,036 Btu per cubic foot.
natural_gas_heat_content_mmbtu_per_mcf.note: Your gas bill states your own heat content (the 'Btu factor' or 'therm factor').

natural_gas_price_per_mmbtu.label: US average natural gas industrial price, 2025, converted to $/MMBtu
natural_gas_price_per_mmbtu.cite: US EIA natural gas industrial price, U.S., / EIA heat content
natural_gas_price_per_mmbtu.source: US EIA, Natural Gas Prices (annual), U.S., 'Industrial Price', 2025: 5.23 dollars per thousand cubic feet (page release date 9/30/2026); divided by the EIA 2025 US heat content of gas delivered to consumers (1,036 Btu/cf).
natural_gas_price_per_mmbtu.note: EIA's industrial price covers only gas sold by local distribution companies: the same table gives 13.4% as the share of total industrial deliveries included in the 2025 price. Most industrial gas is bought from marketers under contracts, so your delivered price (commodity plus transport) may differ widely.

boiler_efficiency.unit: fraction (fuel HHV in to useful heat or steam out)
boiler_efficiency.label: Thermal efficiency EPA assumes for natural-gas-fired steam or heat generation
boiler_efficiency.cite: US EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub, Table 7 note
boiler_efficiency.source: US EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub (2025), Table 7 Steam and Heat, note: 'These factors assume natural gas fuel is used to generate steam or heat at 80 percent thermal efficiency.'
boiler_efficiency.note: An inventory assumption, not a measured boiler. DOE Steam Tip Sheet #15 Table 2 instead lists 85.7% COMBUSTION efficiency for natural gas, for boilers with economizers or air preheaters and 3% flue O2; combustion efficiency excludes shell and blowdown losses, so it is not the same quantity. Use your own boiler's tested fuel-to-steam efficiency.

steam_energy_btu_per_lb.unit: Btu/lb (heat input to make 1 lb of saturated steam from feedwater)
steam_energy_btu_per_lb.label: Energy required to produce one pound of saturated steam (enthalpy of saturated steam minus enthalpy of feedwater)
steam_energy_btu_per_lb.cite: US DOE Steam Tip Sheet #15, Table 1
steam_energy_btu_per_lb.table_keys: operating pressure in psig; values align with feedwater_temps_F
steam_energy_btu_per_lb.interpolation: estimate_impact.py looks up only these three pressures; between tabulated feedwater temperatures (50-250 F) it interpolates linearly (DOE's own worked example uses 1,006 Btu/lb at 450 psig and 230 F, which is the linear interpolation). Outside the table it refuses and asks for your value.
steam_energy_btu_per_lb.source: US DOE Advanced Manufacturing Office, Energy Tips: STEAM, Steam Tip Sheet #15 'Benchmark the Fuel Cost of Steam Generation', Table 1 'Energy Required to Produce One Pound of Saturated Steam, Btu' ('Calculated from steam tables based on the difference between the enthalpies of saturated steam and feedwater'). DOE/GO-102012-3391, January 2012.
steam_energy_btu_per_lb.note: Saturated steam only. Superheated steam, steam lost at a pressure not tabulated, or makeup water colder or warmer than the feedwater temperature you name all need your own steam-table value.

not_included.reason: No national typical value is meaningful: demand charges, ratchets and billing intervals are set by each utility's tariff. The tool never defaults it; take it from your bill or rate schedule.

not_included.item: Steam energy per lb at pressures other than 150, 450 and 600 psig, or for superheated steam
not_included.reason: The only federal steam table checked for this file (DOE Steam Tip Sheet #15) tabulates these three saturated pressures. A full steam table (for example NIST) was outside the sources allowed for this check, so other conditions need your own steam-table value.

not_included.item: Prices of fuels other than natural gas
not_included.reason: Not fetched and verified for this file. Supply your own fuel price for oil, propane or coal.

not_included.item: Marginal or non-baseload grid emission rates for avoided-emissions estimates
not_included.reason: eGRID publishes non-baseload rates in the same table, but choosing a marginal method is an accounting decision for the user (EPA's AVERT is the tool built for it). The default here is the location-based average rate only.

not_included.item: Steam loss per failed trap and air leak rates per orifice
not_included.reason: These are measured quantities, never defaults. DOE Steam Tip Sheet #1 and Compressed Air Tip Sheet #3 print orifice tables, but those are credited to the Boiler Efficiency Institute and the Compressed Air Challenge, and a survey of your own traps or leaks is the measurement.
